premises.text: Cash remittances force recipients into agency travel, long waits, bill-pay trips, and high Western Union fees
premises.evidence_span: They have to pay for a bus to go to an agency, wait online for two hours, then go to another agency to pay their utility bills

premises.text: Immigrants send SMS-usable credit to family phones in Latin America for food, medicine, utilities, and tuition
premises.evidence_span: hardworking immigrants can send a credit directly to their family cell phone in Latin America

premises.text: Senders use online or ~200 mom-and-pop partner stores; recipients redeem via SMS PIN like a gift card
premises.evidence_span: her sister gets a unique SMS pin code that she can use to pay for food at the local supermarket

premises.text: Recipients can transfer part of funds onward, making the remittance experience inherently viral
premises.evidence_span: transfer part of those funds to a family member or another friend

premises.text: Contracts already cover 7,200 retail locations in eight countries enabling LatAm scale
premises.evidence_span: we already have the contracts that gives us access to 7,200 retail locations in eight different countries

premises.text: Retailer fees subsidize a $3 flat customer fee up to 70% cheaper than alternatives
premises.evidence_span: a low flat fee of just $3, up to 70% cheaper than any alternative

value.text: Let immigrants pay for family's basic needs back home via SMS remittance
value.evidence_span: We allow immigrants to pay for all of their family's basic needs back home, all via an SMS

causal_links.evidence_span: pay for food, medicine, utility bills, even tuition
We are building a social network on top of the remittance experience
subsidize how much we charge our customers

notes: Traction metrics (67% WoW, 5,000 customers) excluded as evidence of past performance. $69B LatAm remittance figure used as market context for scale premise via retail contracts. Vision 'future of global remittances' not coded as premise.
